subject: physics
question_text: When are two vectors said to be equal vectors?

verification.note: Sourced from the March 2026 AP Inter Physics Paper-I (NEW) scan held in the corpus — Section A, question 7, read directly off the paper. Neither the Sri Chaitanya Fastrack nor the TSBIE Basic Learning Material lists this question for Unit 4. AP Section A carries 1 mark; this card is authored at the TS 2-mark VSAQ length because the bank is TS-shaped and TS has no 1-mark section. The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The condition
lines: Two vectors are said to be equal when they have
the SAME magnitude and the SAME direction.
Both conditions must hold together — equal
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both conditions in one sentence. Magnitude alone does not earn it.
steps.why: A vector carries exactly two pieces of information, so matching both of them is the whole test.
common_mistakes: Calling two vectors equal because their magnitudes are equal, ignoring direction.

recall.must_convey: That two vectors are equal when they have the same magnitude and the same direction.
reject: they need not act at the same point

steps.memory_tip: Two 5 N forces, one east and one west, are not equal vectors. Same size, opposite direction.

steps.label: What does not matter

lines.text: Equal vectors need not act at the same point.

lines: A vector may be shifted parallel to itself
without changing it, so two equal vectors can
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say that the point of application does not matter.
steps.why: This is exactly why vectors can be slid head to tail to add them — position carries no information at all.
common_mistakes: Requiring the two vectors to start from the same point.

recall.must_convey: That equal vectors need not act at the same point, since a vector can be shifted parallel to itself.
accept: need not act at the same point
can be shifted parallel to itself

steps.memory_tip: Two arrows at opposite corners of the page are still equal if length and direction match.

insider_note: Asked in AP March 2026, Section A. Two marks for two sentences, and the second — that position does not matter — is the one usually left out.
